title: Scientists and ethical discipline
competency: Appreciate the work of world and Ethiopian scientists and explain why ethics matter in science.

keywords.def: Someone who gathers evidence in an orderly way, makes hypotheses, tests them, and shares what is learned.
The principles of right and wrong that guide how scientists behave, such as honesty and responsibility.
A substance that kills snails. Endod berries are a strong, cheap and safe molluscicide.

en.text: A scientist gathers evidence in an orderly way, tests ideas and shares knowledge. World scientists include Newton, Curie, Faraday and Einstein. Ethiopian scientists include Dr. Aklilu Lemma, who found that endod kills the snails that spread bilharzia, and Dr. Gebisa Ejeta, known for sorghum.

am.text: ሳይንቲስት ማስረጃን በሥርዓት ይሰበስባል፣ ሐሳቦችን ይፈትሻል፣ እውቀትንም ያካፍላል። የዓለም ሳይንቲስቶች ኒውተን፣ ኩሪ፣ ፋራዴይና አንስታይን ናቸው። ከኢትዮጵያ ሳይንቲስቶች ዶ/ር አክሊሉ ለማ እንዶድ ቢልሃርዝያን የሚያስተላልፉ ቀንድ አውጣዎችን እንደሚገድል አግኝተዋል፤ ዶ/ር ገቢሳ እጀታ በማሽላ ሥራቸው ይታወቃሉ።

screens.title: A plant against disease
screens.text: Bilharzia is a disease spread by a tiny worm. The worm lives part of its life in water snails.
screens.ask: How could a plant help stop bilharzia?
screens.after:
The worm needs water snails for part of its life.
If the snails die, the worm cannot grow and spread.
So a plant that kills snails can stop bilharzia.
An Ethiopian scientist found such a plant: endod. Read on.

screens.title: What is a scientist?
paras: A scientist systematically gathers and uses research and evidence.
A scientist makes hypotheses and tests them. The aim is to gain and share understanding and knowledge.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Someone who gathers evidence in an orderly way, makes hypotheses, tests them, and shares what is learned.

screens.title: What scientists do
screens.text: What scientists do: which of these is the work of a scientist?
opts: Gathering evidence, testing hypotheses and sharing knowledge
screens.ans: Gathering evidence, testing hypotheses and sharing knowledge
screens.why:
Step 1: a scientist gathers research and evidence in an orderly way.
Step 2: a scientist makes hypotheses and tests them.
Step 3: the aim is to gain and share knowledge.
So the answer is gathering evidence, testing hypotheses and sharing knowledge.
"Keeping results secret" is wrong: scientists share what they learn.

people.name: Marie Curie
people.did: Discovered the elements polonium and radium. Won Nobel Prizes in 1903 and 1911.

people.name: Isaac Newton
people.did: Discovered the laws of motion and the law of gravity.

people.name: Michael Faraday
people.did: Made electricity from magnetism. Built the first dynamo.

people.name: Albert Einstein
people.did: Developed the theory of special relativity.

screens.title: Motion and gravity
screens.text: World scientists: which scientist discovered the laws of motion and the law of gravity?
screens.why:
Look at "World scientists".
Isaac Newton (1643–1727) of England discovered the laws of motion and gravity.
Einstein developed special relativity. Faraday made electricity from magnetism. Curie discovered polonium and radium.
So the answer is Isaac Newton.

people.name: Dr. Aklilu Lemma
people.did: Found a natural treatment for schistosomiasis (bilharzia, snail fever) in 1964.

people.name: Prof. Yalemtsehay Mekonnen
people.did: Studies human physiology, pesticides and health, and plants as medicine. First female professor of Addis Ababa University.

people.name: Dr. Tewolde Berhan Gebre Egziabher
people.did: Worked to protect biodiversity and communities' rights to their genetic resources.

people.name: Dr. Gebisa Ejeta
people.did: Plant breeder and geneticist. Won the 2009 World Food Prize for hybrid sorghum for Africa.

screens.title: How endod helps
paras: Endod berries are used for soap and shampoo in many parts of Africa.
They are a strong, cheap and safe molluscicide (snail killer). This stops the parasitic worm spreading.

screens.title: How endod stops bilharzia
steps: The bilharzia worm lives part of its life in water snails.
From the snails, the worm gets into people who touch the water.
Dr. Aklilu Lemma found that endod berries kill these snails.
No snails means the worm cannot complete its life.
So the disease stops spreading. Endod is strong, cheap and safe.

screens.title: How endod helps
screens.text: Dr. Aklilu Lemma's endod discovery helps prevent bilharzia.
opts: Endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease
screens.ans: Endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease
screens.why:
Step 1: the bilharzia worm lives part of its life in water snails.
Step 2: endod berries are a molluscicide: they kill snails.
Step 3: with no snails, the worm cannot spread.
So endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease.
screens.clue: What does a molluscicide kill? (Bilharzia is also called snail fever.)
screens.ask: How does the endod discovery help prevent bilharzia?

screens.title: Protecting biodiversity
screens.text: Ethiopian scientists: who worked to protect biodiversity and communities' rights to their genetic resources?
screens.why:
Compare the Ethiopian scientists.
Dr. Aklilu Lemma → endod against bilharzia.
Dr. Gebisa Ejeta → sorghum, World Food Prize.
Prof. Yalemtsehay Mekonnen → physiology and plants as medicine.
Dr. Tewolde Berhan Gebre Egziabher → biodiversity and communities' rights.
So the answer is Dr. Tewolde Berhan Gebre Egziabher.
screens.clue: Compare the Ethiopian scientists in the reading.

screens.title: A prize for food
screens.ask: Ethiopian scientists: Dr. Gebisa Ejeta won the World Food Prize in 2009 for his work on ___.
screens.why:
Dr. Gebisa Ejeta is a plant breeder and geneticist.
He won the 2009 World Food Prize.
It was for hybrid sorghum for Africa.
So the answer is sorghum (mashila).
screens.clue: It is a grain crop. In Amharic it is called mashila.
screens.worked:
Step 1: the reading says Dr. Gebisa Ejeta is a plant breeder.
Step 2: he won the World Food Prize in 2009.
Step 3: the prize was for hybrid sorghum for Africa.
So the answer is sorghum (mashila in Amharic).

en.text: Ethics are the principles of right and wrong that guide scientists. They keep science honest, careful and fair, so results can be trusted. Scientific codes address honesty, responsibility, objectivity, openness, competence, legality, non-discrimination and carefulness.

am.text: ሥነ ምግባር ሳይንቲስቶችን የሚመሩ የትክክልና የስሕተት መርሆዎች ናቸው። ሳይንስን ታማኝ፣ ጥንቁቅና ፍትሐዊ ያደርጋሉ፤ ውጤቶችም እንዲታመኑ ያደርጋሉ። ሳይንሳዊ ደንቦች ታማኝነትን፣ ኃላፊነትን፣ ገለልተኝነትን፣ ግልጽነትን፣ ብቃትን፣ ሕጋዊነትን፣ አለማዳላትንና ጥንቃቄን ይመለከታሉ።

screens.title: A different result
screens.text: Your group in the school lab got a result that is different from the book.
screens.ask: What should you write in your report?
screens.after:
Honest scientists write what they really measured.
A different result can teach something: maybe a mistake, maybe something new.
Copying the book's answer hides the truth.
Read on about ethics in science.

screens.title: Ethical principles in science
paras: Ethics are an essential part of science. Like science, ethics must be consistent and justified.
We must judge what is right or wrong, good or bad. Scientific codes address these principles: honesty, responsibility, objectivity, openness, competence, legality, non-discrimination, carefulness.

screens.title: The eight ethical principles
screens.ask: Tap each principle to see what it means at school.
items: Tell the truth about your methods and results. At school: Write the readings you really measured.
Take care for your work and how it affects people and the environment. At school: Clean up and dispose of waste properly.
Judge by the evidence, not by what you wish were true. At school: Report a result even if it shows your idea was wrong.
Share your methods and results and listen to others. At school: Let classmates check your experiment.
Know how to do the work well and keep learning. At school: Learn how to use an apparatus before you use it.
Follow the rules and laws that apply to your work. At school: Follow the lab rules.
Treat everyone fairly. At school: Every member of the group gets a turn.
Work carefully and check your work to avoid mistakes. At school: Measure twice and record neatly.

screens.title: Name it
defs: The principles of right and wrong that guide how scientists behave, such as honesty and responsibility.

screens.title: Sharing methods
screens.text: A scientist shares her methods so that others can repeat her experiment.
screens.why:
Step 1: what does she do? She shares her methods.
Step 2: openness means sharing methods and results and listening to others.
Step 3: then others can repeat and check her experiment.
So the answer is openness.
Carefulness is about checking your own work, not sharing it.
screens.clue: Find the principle about sharing in the table.
screens.ask: Ethical principles: which principle is shown by sharing methods so others can repeat the work?

screens.title: Double-checking
screens.text: A student double-checks every reading before writing it down.
screens.why:
Step 1: the student checks each reading twice.
Step 2: that avoids mistakes.
Step 3: carefulness means working carefully and checking to avoid mistakes.
So the answer is carefulness.
screens.clue: Which principle is about avoiding mistakes?
screens.ask: Ethical principles: which principle is shown by double-checking every reading?

screens.title: Changing the results
screens.text: Selam's measurements do not match the book. She changes her numbers so they match.
screens.why:
Step 1: Selam's real numbers differ from the book.
Step 2: she writes numbers she did not measure.
Step 3: honesty means telling the truth about methods and results.
So she breaks honesty.
The right thing: report the real numbers and discuss why they differ.
screens.clue: Which principle is about telling the truth?
screens.ask: Which ethical principle is she breaking?
screens.worked:
Step 1: Selam wrote numbers she did not really measure.
Step 2: honesty means telling the truth about your results.
Step 3: a different result is allowed; a false result is not.
So she breaks the principle of honesty.

screens.title: Evidence first
screens.ask: Ethical principles: judging by the evidence, not by what you wish were true, is called ___.
screens.why:
Think of the eight principles.
One is about evidence, not wishes.
It means you report a result even if it shows your idea was wrong.
That principle is objectivity.
screens.clue: Look at the third row of the table.

items.why:
Interacting: the sciences work together.
Interrelated: their ideas are linked.
Overlapping: there is no clear border line between them.
All three words are true.
So the answer is "All of the above".
items.clue: Is only one of these words true?

items.text: The branches of natural science that study the composition of compounds and the processes in organisms are:
items.why:
Step 1: composition of compounds is about substances → chemistry.
Step 2: processes in organisms are about living things → biology.
So the answer is chemistry and biology.
Geology studies the earth, so options with geology are wrong.
items.clue: Which branch studies substances? Which studies living things?

opts: It is the study of the physical and natural world
It comes from the Latin word "scientia", meaning knowledge
It is a system of gaining knowledge using the scientific method
items.why:
Check each statement against 1.1.1.
"Study of the physical and natural world": true.
"From the Latin scientia, meaning knowledge": true.
"A system of gaining knowledge using the scientific method": true.
All three are true, so the answer is "All are correct".

items.text: Which is true about indigenous knowledge?
opts: It is based on the scientific method
It is knowledge derived from western countries
It has a universal view and is commonly recognised as western science
items.why:
Step 1: indigenous knowledge is built by local people from long experience.
Step 2: so it incorporates local people's knowledge.
Step 3: the scientific method and "western science" describe conventional science.
So the answer is: it incorporates local people's knowledge.

items.text: Which world-famous scientist discovered the law of motion and gravity?
items.why:
Isaac Newton (1643–1727, England) discovered the laws of motion and the law of gravity.
Einstein: special relativity. Faraday: electricity from magnetism. Curie: polonium and radium.
So the answer is Isaac Newton.
items.clue: Look back at "World scientists" in this section.

test.text: Who discovered a natural treatment for bilharzia (schistosomiasis) in 1964?
test.why:
Dr. Aklilu Lemma found a natural treatment for bilharzia in 1964.
He found that endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease.
Dr. Gebisa Ejeta worked on sorghum, not bilharzia.
So the answer is Dr. Aklilu Lemma.

test.ask: World scientists: Michael Faraday discovered how to make electricity from ___.
test.why:
Look at Michael Faraday in "World scientists".
He made electricity from magnetism.
He built the first dynamo, a machine that does this.
So the answer is magnetism.

test.text: Why ethics matter: ethics help keep scientific work honest, careful and fair, so results can be trusted.
test.why:
Ethics are principles of right and wrong in science.
They include honesty, carefulness and non-discrimination (fairness).
When work is honest and careful, others can trust the results.
So the statement is true.
